To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the application of about one hundred known triplet phases at 2.5 A resolution, assumed known with an average error of about +/-20 degrees, was sufficient to initiate the solution of a protein structure, and that the use of these triplet phases in the refinement of the protein structure at 2 A resolution was sufficient to reduce the error in the triplet phases from +/- 20 degrees to about +/- 10 degrees.

(1) the application of triplet phases, known to a precision of about +/- 10 degrees, to the determination of protein crystal structures is feasible, (2) the use of these phases in combination with single-phase techniques, such as tangent formula estimation, is effective in the solution of protein crystal structures, (3) the use of triplet phases, in combination with partial structure, is effective for the refinement of protein crystal structures.

(1) triplet phases are known to a precision of +/- 20 degrees or so; (2) the mean direction of triplet phases is shifted by 0.1-0.2 A; (3) the concentration parameter is enhanced by a factor of 2-3; and (4) the a priori triplet phases are sufficient to initiate the solution of a structure at 2 A resolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of known triplet phases to the study of the structure of a protein.
the development of methods for the solution of crystallographic structures from data at low resolution.
the application of triplet phases in crystallographic analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of triplet phases in this case was a very powerful and effective tool in the solution of a protein structure.
direct methods are a powerful tool for structure determination, but that they require a substantial amount of a priori phase information.
the triplet phases were essential for the solution of the structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a priori triplet phases is an effective means to solve a structure, and the method can be applied with confidence at 1.8 A resolution.
the use of known triplet phases has been a useful tool in the study of small protein crystals.
the use of a priori triplet phases is an efficient way to solve a structure at high resolution and to refine it to high accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
triplet phases can be used to enhance the convergence of the direct methods solution of a structure, even when the resolution is as low as 2.0 Angstrom.

the application of known triplet phases, even at low resolution, can be used to initiate solution of a structure and to provide a starting point from which a complete structure solution can be obtained.
triplet phases, when known with sufficient reliability, can be applied directly in the refinement process.
